title: Limited Drop Alert Video Template | AIVideosUGC
description: Drive urgency for a small release or restock with a drop alert video from one product photo. Add your date, quantity and notify link after download.
h1: Limited Drop Alert Video for a Restock or Small Release
lead: Place the release product in a scene, add a voiceover and captions, and put the date on only after download.
steps_h2: Make a Limited Release Ad in 3 Steps
steps_lead: The scene shows the product. Add the spoken line here, and keep the date and quantity editable after download.

steps.d: Upload one clear photo of the item in the drop, or paste its product page link.
Name the reveal and a short spoken line, then pick a size and a length from 6 to 30 seconds.
Download the alert, add the date and quantity, and publish it to TikTok or Meta. Pause it when stock runs out.

faq.q: What is a limited drop alert video?
faq.a: A ready scene for a short release. You add your product photo, a hook, a script, and a voiceover, and an AI actor can hold the item. You type the date and the quantity after download.

faq.q: How do I build the alert?
faq.a: Upload the photo or paste a product page link, take the script, pick an AI actor and a voiceover, choose a size and a length, then download. You can make several openings from that same photo.

faq.q: Why start from a product photo instead of filming the drop?
faq.a: The scene comes from the photo or the product link, so you can prepare the alert before the release without booking a creator for every colorway.

faq.q: Who is a shoe drop video for?
faq.a: Shops with a short release window, including shoe drops, apparel, a beauty shade, or a home restock, on TikTok, Reels, or a product page.

faq.q: Can a first-time seller use it?
faq.a: Yes. One clear photo and a short line are enough. Captions, music, and the spoken line can be set before you download.

faq.q: Can the clip show a live countdown or the stock count?
faq.a: Add the countdown, date, and quantity as text after download. The tool does not keep a clock or a stock number in sync with your store.

faq.q: Which size and length fit a drop post?
faq.a: 9:16 for TikTok and Reels, 1:1 for a feed, plus 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4. Lengths are 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. You can publish the file to TikTok or Meta.

faq.q: Does it include music, captions, or a voiceover?
faq.a: Yes. Set a voiceover, captions, and a track from the music library in the built-in editor. You can speak the line again in another language.

24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, and 120 for 30. You see the cost first, and a failed job returns its credits. Plans start at $24.50 a month. There is no free plan. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: What should I do when the drop sells out?
faq.a: Pause or replace the ad and change the quantity line. A catalog API can start the next alert from your store. Any person on screen is an AI actor, not a buyer.

steps.sourceHint: Show the full shoe shape and color in a clear view.
steps.prompt: An adult hiker ties the coral trail shoes on a rocky trail, then stands so the tread and both shoes stay in frame. Leave room above the shoes for a date you add after download.

reviews.h2: Shops Are Switching to Shoe Drop Videos
reviews.lead: Example ways a shop makes a limited drop alert video. The date and the stock note still go on after download.

items.t: A finished alert from one product photo
items.d: Example: a watch shop uploads the caseback and gets a short limited drop alert video it can post. The release date is typed on later.

items.t: The still and the clip in one project
items.d: Example: an apparel shop builds the jacket photo and the restock alert together, on a first try, without opening a second app.

items.t: Hold the pair, or start from the link
items.d: Example: a shoe shop pastes the product page link, or uploads the pair, and the clip shows those shoes held up for the drop.

items.t: An AI actor, then captions in the editor
items.d: Example: the shop picks an AI actor from the actor library to hold the jacket, trims the clip in the editor, and sets captions.

items.t: The same drop in another language
items.d: Example: a beauty shop keeps one shade reveal and speaks the line again in a second language for the other market.

items.t: A track and a spoken line before download
items.d: Example: a home shop adds a voiceover and a track from the music library, then edits both before the candle restock goes out.

items.t: An AI actor instead of a booked creator
items.d: Example: a bag shop uses an AI actor for the first turn of a small run. Someone new to video can start from one photo.

items.t: A digital twin skips another light setup
items.d: Example: a drink shop uses a digital twin for the flavor hold, so the team does not rebuild the set for every new can.

items.t: A script, a voice, and a second opening
items.d: Example: a jewelry shop pastes the product link, takes the script and the voiceover, then makes a second opening from the same photo.

items.t: Publish to TikTok or Meta, or use the API
items.d: Example: a fitness shop publishes the gear alert to TikTok or Meta from the project. A catalog API can start the next one.
